extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents) involved in appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and required content for an examiner's answer to an appeal brief before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, including what must be stated, how rejections must be explained, and limits on new grounds of rejection. Focused on preparing, formatting, and justifying an examiner's answer and related procedural steps (entry of amendments, reopening prosecution, citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 1.192 for briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs must comply with 37 CFR 1.192; if the brief fails to address any or all grounds of rejection advanced by the examiner, or comply with 37 CFR 1.192(c), the indicated procedure set forth in MPEP § 1206 under 'Review of Brief by Examiner' should be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a brief does not meet 1.192 requirements, examiner follows MPEP §1206 procedures (e.g., notify appellant, require corrected brief). If appellant fails to describe the invention as required by 37 CFR 1.192, the examiner is not required to provide those omissions under 1.192(d), though the examiner should clarify the description in the answer if necessary to present the case properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required headings and items in examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's answer is required to include, under appropriate headings, in the order indicated, the following items: (1) Real Party in Interest; (2) Related Appeals and Interferences; (3) Status of Claims; (4) Status of Amendments After Final; (5) Summary of Invention; (6) Issues; (7) Grouping of Claims; (8) Claims Appealed; (9) References of Record; (10) Grounds of Rejection; (11) Response to Argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified headings and order. Follow form paragraphs provided (¶12.49, ¶12.50, etc.) and attach or use appropriate sub-paragraphs where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party in Interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer must contain a statement acknowledging identification of the real party in financial interest or indicating that the party named in the caption of the brief is the real party in interest; if no identification, state it is presumed the caption name is the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will presume the caption name is the real party in interest but the Board may require an explicit statement from appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals and interferences statement
rubrics_metrics.description: State acknowledgment of appellant's identification of related cases which will directly affect or be directly affected by the decision, or if none identified, state the presumption that there are none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may exercise discretion to require explicit statement if appellant's brief omitted this information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims statement
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the examiner agrees or disagrees with the statement of the status of claims in the brief and provide a correct statement of the status of all claims pending or cancelled, if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner considers some or all finally rejected claims are allowable, follow MPEP § 1208.02. Use follow-up form paragraphs (12.51.01–12.51.10) to indicate agreements, disagreements, claims on appeal, substituted/amended claims, allowed claims, objected-to claims, withdrawn claims, and canceled claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the examiner disagrees with the appellant's statement of the status of amendments after final rejection and identify status of all amendments submitted after final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs (¶12.52.01–12.52.05) to indicate entered/not entered/no amendments; identify dates of amendments and whether they were entered or denied entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of invention statement
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the examiner disagrees with the summary of invention contained in the brief and, if deficient, explain the deficiency and include a correct summary if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the summary is deficient, explain specifics (¶12.53.02). Include a correct summary when necessary for clear understanding of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues statement (appealable vs petitionable)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the examiner disagrees with the statement of the issues in the brief and explain the reasons, including identification of any issues which are petitionable rather than appealable and any grounds of rejection the examiner no longer considers applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶12.54 series; explicitly identify petitionable subjects under 37 CFR 1.181 and explain any changes to appellant's stated issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of claims: stand-or-fall grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the examiner disagrees with any statement that certain claims do not stand or fall together and provide explanation why those claims are not separately patentable if disagreeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant did not include required statement/reasons in brief (37 CFR 1.192(c)(7)), notify appellant of non-compliance using form paragraphs 12.69, 12.69.01 and 12.78. Use ¶12.55.01/02/04 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appealed and correctness of appendix copy
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the copy of the appealed claims in the appendix to the brief is correct and, if not, provide a correct copy of any incorrect claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If minor errors exist, indicate them and attach corrected claim(s); if errors are substantial, require a corrected brief and potentially other form paragraphs (12.69, 12.77, 12.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: References of record listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a listing of the references of record relied upon, and for nonpatent references include the relevant page(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified format for each cited reference (number, name, date) and follow examples in MPEP § 707.05(e). Maintain soft copies/prints of references in file wrapper when forwarding files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection: explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of rejection applicable to the appealed claims, provide an explanation of the ground of rejection or reference to a final rejection or other single prior action for a clear exposition of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain each ground fully or point to a single prior action that does. If pointing to a prior action, ensure the prior action fully sets forth the rejection; otherwise supply the full explanation in the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the examiner's answer (or single prior action) shall explain how the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is not complied with, including how the specification/drawings (a) do not describe the subject matter defined by each rejected claim, (b) would not enable one skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter without undue experimentation, and (c) do not set forth the best mode contemplated by the appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific references to specification/drawings and explain the deficiency claim-by-claim as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the examiner's answer (or single prior action) shall explain how the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify claim language that is indefinite or fails the 'particular' and 'distinct' requirement and explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102 anticipation explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the examiner's answer (or single prior action) shall explain why the rejected claims are anticipated or not patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102, pointing out where all specific limitations recited in the rejected claims are found in the prior art relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to exact locations in the prior art (page/line/drawing) where each limitation is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103 obviousness explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner's answer (or single prior action) shall (i) state the ground of rejection and point out where each specific limitation is found in the prior art relied upon, (ii) identify any differences between the rejected claims and the prior art relied on, and (iii) explain how and why the claimed subject matter is rendered unpatentable over the prior art. If based on combination of references, explain the rationale for making the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a reasoned explanation tying claim limitations to references and rationale for combining teachings when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-by-feature comparison when correspondence unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are questions as to how limitations in the claims correspond to features in the prior art even after complying with 102/103 explanation requirements, the examiner shall compare at least one rejected claim feature-by-feature with the prior art relied on in the rejection, aligning the claim language side-by-side with references to specific page/line/drawing/quotation as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed side-by-side alignment for at least one claim to remove ambiguity about correspondences between claim language and prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirement for other rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection other than those under the specific paragraphs for 112, 102, 103, the examiner's answer (or single prior action) shall specifically explain the basis for the particular rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the explanation to the statutory or rule basis of the rejection (e.g., statutory subject-matter, enablement variations, statutory bars) with specific supporting facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to appellant's arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer should state whether the examiner disagrees with each of appellant's contentions presented in the brief and provide explanations of the reasons for disagreement with any such contention. If any ground of rejection is not argued and replied to by appellant, the response shall point out each claim affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address each contention in the brief; include necessary rebuttal and indicate the impact on each claim if appellant omitted reply on particular grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may incorporate in the answer their statement of the grounds of rejection merely by reference to the final rejection (or a single other action). Only those statements of grounds of rejection appearing in a single prior action may be incorporated by reference; an answer should not refer, directly or indirectly, to more than one prior Office action. The page and paragraph of the final action or other single prior action to be incorporated should be explicitly identified. Statements of grounds of rejection appearing in actions other than that single prior action should be quoted in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If further explanation of the rejection is necessary, include it in the answer rather than over-broadly incorporating multiple prior actions by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific MPEP form paragraphs (e.g., ¶12.49, ¶12.50, ¶12.50.01–.06, ¶12.51–¶12.57, ¶12.59, ¶12.61, ¶12.79, ¶12.81, etc.) should be used as provided for standard content and boilerplate in the examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow bracket insertion instructions in form paragraphs for paper numbers, application number, filing date, appellant name, representative name, and dates. Use form paragraphs appropriate to the situation (typed answer vs typist, admissions, disagreements, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against new ground of rejection in examiner's answer (37 CFR 1.193(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2) prohibits the entry of a new ground of rejection in an examiner's answer. If a new ground of rejection is necessary at answer time, prosecution must be reopened and supervisory approval obtained prior to reopening prosecution after an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no new ground when the basic thrust/statutory basis and evidence remain the same (In re Kronig). A change in rationale/discussion alone does not necessarily constitute a new ground. If reopening prosecution is necessary, obtain supervisory approval per MPEP §1002.02(d). Use ¶12.81 form paragraph when reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner's answer may include rejections of claims added/ amended under 37 CFR 1.116
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 proposes to add/amend claims, appellant was advised by advisory action that the amendment would be entered for appeal, and the advisory action indicates which individual rejection(s) set forth in the action from which appeal has been taken would be used to reject the added or amended claims, then (1) the appeal brief must address those rejection(s) and (2) the examiner's answer may include the rejection(s) of the added or amended claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing of such an amendment represents appellant's consent to proceed with appeal process. However, whether the amendment is entitled to entry is controlled by 37 CFR 1.116 (not 1.193). If more than a mere reference to prior rejections is necessary to explain how added/amended claims would be rejected, deny entry as raising new issues requiring further consideration/search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on combining individual rejections for amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2) authorizes rejection in an examiner's answer of a claim that combines limitations previously rejected individually only to the extent that the advisory action identified the specific individual rejection(s) that would be used; combining multiple individual rejections into a new combined rejection (e.g., using A in view of B and C) where that combined rejection was not indicated may constitute a new ground and is not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: combining claim 1 and 2 may be authorized if advisory action indicated that rejection; combining claims 1,2,3 into a new claim raising new issues may be refused entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of new prior art in examiner's answer generally constitutes new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A new prior art reference cited for the first time in an examiner's answer generally will constitute a new ground of rejection. If citation of a new reference is necessary to support a rejection, it must be included in the statement of rejection (which would introduce a new ground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new reference is added merely as evidence of a prior well-known statement by the examiner, its citation in the answer may not constitute a new ground. If an allegation that an answer contains an impermissible new ground is not timely raised by petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a), it is waived (37 CFR 1.181(f)). See MPEP §2144.03 and In re Hoch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should reevaluate position and withdraw non-adhered rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should reevaluate his or her position in light of the arguments presented in the brief, and should expressly withdraw any rejections not adhered to, especially if the rejection was made in an action which is incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though the Board may treat unmentioned rejections as withdrawn, explicitly withdraw them in the answer when appropriate (see Ex parte Emm). Include any necessary rebuttal of arguments presented in the appellant's brief if the final action does not adequately meet the arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: All correspondence must be on the record; unpublished decisions limited
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence with the Board, whether by the examiner or the appellant, must be on the record. Unpublished decisions unavailable to the public by reason of 35 U.S.C. 122 cannot be cited by examiner or appellant except where the decision is in an application having common ownership with the application on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner's answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of patent law, forward examiner's answer, application file, and explanatory memorandum to the Group Director for consideration; if approved, forward to Office of Deputy Assistant Commissioner for Patent Policy and Projects for final approval (see MPEP §1003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward examiner's answer when it contains new legal interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner's answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of existing patent law, the examiner's answer, application file, and explanatory memorandum should be forwarded to the Group Director for consideration; if approved, forward to the Office of the Deputy Assistant Commissioner for Patent Policy and Projects for final approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures supervisory review of novel legal positions taken in answers. See MPEP §1003.
